generality.prompt: Is the construction stated over an arbitrary base scheme \(S\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction is functorial in \(S\); a fixed base ring is a special case obtained by setting \(S = \operatorname{Spec} R\).

nodes.title: Points of 𝔾_a Are the Additive Group of R

generality.prompt: Does the formula apply to arbitrary commutative \(k\)-algebras \(R\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The formula \(\mathbb{G}_a(R) = (R, +)\) is natural in any commutative algebra \(R\) over the base.

nodes.title: Affine Algebraic Groups

generality.prompt: Is this stated for affine group schemes over a base scheme, not just over a field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The constructions and theorems are stated over an arbitrary base; the field case is the special case `S = Spec k`.

nodes.title: Affine Group Scheme over a Base

generality.prompt: Is this definition stated for an arbitrary base scheme \(S\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The base \(S\) is an arbitrary scheme; specialization to \(S = \operatorname{Spec} k\) or \(S = \operatorname{Spec} O_F\) is left to consumers.

nodes.title: Composition with the Antipode Is an Algebra Hom for Commutative Hopf Algebras

generality.prompt: Is this node aligned with the Lean result currently used for affine group coordinate rings?
generality.verdict: Yes. The formalized project theorem assumes the Hopf algebra A is commutative and the target B is commutative; the more general noncommutative-source variant is deferred to the general antipode anti-multiplicativity node.

nodes.title: Convolution of Algebra Homomorphisms

generality.prompt: Is the definition stated at the right level — bialgebra source, commutative target — to support the group-structure construction?
generality.verdict: Yes. The bialgebra structure on \(A\) provides comultiplication; the commutativity of \(B\) is what makes the convolution of two algebra homomorphisms again an algebra homomorphism.

nodes.title: Algebra Homomorphisms Form a Group Under Convolution

generality.prompt: Is the statement at the right level — Hopf source, commutative target — and is the group commutative when the bialgebra is cocommutative?
generality.verdict: Yes. The Hopf hypothesis is essential for inverses; commutativity of B is essential for the convolution to land in algebra homs. The convolution group is commutative iff A is cocommutative (Δ is symmetric).

nodes.title: Algebraic Group over a Base

generality.prompt: Does the definition follow the modern Milne / SGA 3 convention without smoothness?
generality.verdict: Yes. Smoothness is intentionally not part of the definition; \(\mu_n\) and \(\alpha_p\) in characteristic \(p\) are algebraic groups but not smooth, and we want to admit them as instances.

nodes.title: Antipode of a Hopf Algebra Is Anti-Multiplicative

generality.prompt: Is the lemma stated for arbitrary Hopf algebras (no commutativity assumption)?
generality.verdict: Yes. Anti-multiplicativity holds for every Hopf algebra; the Lean wrapper delegates to Mathlib's ring-theoretic theorem.

nodes.title: Antipode of a Commutative Hopf Algebra Is Multiplicative

generality.prompt: Is the hypothesis 'A is a commutative Hopf algebra' the right level — does the statement fail without commutativity?
generality.verdict: Yes. Without commutativity of A, the antipode is only anti-multiplicative (S(ab) = S(b)S(a)), not multiplicative. Commutativity of A collapses anti-mult to mult. The direct proof below uses commutativity in exactly one Sweedler step.

nodes.title: Base Change

generality.prompt: Does this treatment of base change apply to arbitrary morphisms of base schemes, not just field extensions?
generality.verdict: Yes. The pullback construction works for any morphism `f : T → S`, with the field-extension case being a special case.

nodes.title: Base Change Preserves Algebraic Group Structure

generality.prompt: Is the statement formulated for arbitrary base change morphisms \(f : T \to S\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. No assumption on \(f\) beyond being a morphism of schemes; the proof composes pullback-stability lemmas for each constituent property.

nodes.title: Comodule over a Coalgebra

generality.prompt: Is the definition stated over an arbitrary commutative semiring?
generality.verdict: Yes. The structure makes sense over any commutative semiring \(R\); specialization to a field \(k\) is left to consumers.

nodes.title: Convolution of Algebra Homomorphisms Is an Algebra Homomorphism

generality.prompt: Is the hypothesis 'B commutative' really essential?
generality.verdict: Yes. For non-commutative B, the convolution of two algebra homs is only a linear map, not generally an algebra hom; the proof uses commutativity of B to interchange middle factors. The hypothesis 'A is a bialgebra' is also essential — the algebra-hom property of Δ is what makes f * g respect multiplication.

nodes.title: Coordinate Hopf Algebra of an Affine Group Scheme

generality.prompt: Is the construction stated for affine group schemes over an arbitrary base ring \(R\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. \(R\) is any commutative ring; specialization to a field is left to consumers.

nodes.title: Coordinate Rings and Hopf Algebras

generality.prompt: Does the equivalence hold over an arbitrary commutative base ring, not just a field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The Spec/Γ duality is stated over any commutative base ring `R`; restricting to a field is a special case.

nodes.title: Faithful Linear Representation

generality.prompt: Does the definition allow an arbitrary finite-dimensional representation space \(V\) over the base field?
generality.verdict: Yes. \(V\) is any finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space; the target group scheme is a model of \(\operatorname{GL}(V)\).

nodes.title: Finite-Dimensional Subspace in a Sub-Comodule

generality.prompt: Is the lemma stated with minimal hypotheses?
generality.verdict: Yes. \(A\) need only be a coalgebra over \(k\); finite-generation of \(A\) as an algebra is not used here. The corollary on regular representations uses finite generation.

nodes.title: General Linear Group Scheme GL_n

generality.prompt: Is the construction stated over an arbitrary base scheme \(S\) and arbitrary positive integer \(n\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. \(S\) is any scheme; \(n\) is any positive integer (or any nonempty finite index set).

nodes.title: Points of GL_n Are Invertible n×n Matrices over R

generality.prompt: Does the formula hold for arbitrary commutative \(k\)-algebras \(R\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The formula \(\operatorname{GL}_n(R) = \operatorname{GL}_n(R)\) (invertible matrices over \(R\)) is natural in any commutative algebra \(R\) over the base.

nodes.title: Essential Image of Spec Is Affine Group Schemes

generality.prompt: Is the essential image characterized intrinsically (without finite-type or smoothness)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The characterization is geometric: a group scheme \(G\) is in the essential image iff its underlying scheme is affine. No finite type or smoothness condition.

nodes.title: Spec Functor on Hopf Algebras Is Fully Faithful

generality.prompt: Is the statement formulated for an arbitrary commutative base ring \(R\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The full-faithfulness is a consequence of \(\operatorname{Spec}\) being fully faithful on \(\mathsf{CommRingCat}\) and of \(\operatorname{mapGrp}\) reflecting full-faithfulness.

nodes.title: Spec Functor on Hopf Algebras

generality.prompt: Is the functor defined for an arbitrary commutative base ring \(R\), not only a field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction is over any \(R \in \mathsf{CommRingCat}\); restricting to a field is a special case.

nodes.title: Group Object Structure on Spec A via Yoneda

generality.prompt: Is the construction stated for an arbitrary commutative base ring R?
generality.verdict: Yes. The Yoneda + convolution argument works over any commutative R; specialization to a field is a special case.

nodes.title: Multiplication of a Commutative Bialgebra Is a Coalgebra Hom

generality.prompt: Does this require commutativity of A?
generality.verdict: No — this is a pure bialgebra fact (counit and comul are algebra homomorphisms, by definition of bialgebra). The commutativity of A is not used in this lemma, only in downstream uses like antipode multiplicativity.

nodes.title: Multiplicative Group Scheme 𝔾_m

generality.prompt: Is the construction stated over an arbitrary base scheme \(S\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction is functorial in \(S\); a fixed base ring is the special case \(S = \operatorname{Spec} R\).

nodes.title: Points of 𝔾_m Are the Units of R

generality.prompt: Does the formula hold for arbitrary commutative \(k\)-algebras \(R\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The formula \(\mathbb{G}_m(R) = R^\times\) is natural in any commutative algebra \(R\) over the base.

nodes.title: R-Points of a Group Scheme Form a Group

generality.prompt: Is the statement at the right level: arbitrary \(R\), arbitrary group scheme, abstract group structure?
generality.verdict: Yes. The result is the categorical consequence of \(G\) being a group object; \(R\) and \(G\) are unconstrained beyond the standing assumptions.

nodes.title: Functor of Points of a Group Scheme

generality.prompt: Is the points functor defined for arbitrary \(k\)-algebras \(R\), not only \(R = k\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. \(R\) is any commutative \(k\)-algebra; the \(k\)-points are the special case \(R = k\).

nodes.title: Regular Representation as a Comodule

generality.prompt: Is the example stated over an arbitrary base field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction works over any commutative base ring; only the field case is used by the embedding argument.

nodes.title: G-Representations Are A-Comodules

generality.prompt: Is the equivalence stated for arbitrary \(V\), not only finite-dimensional?
generality.verdict: Yes. The equivalence holds for arbitrary \(k\)-vector spaces \(V\); the finite-dimensional case is the special instance used by the embedding theorem.

nodes.title: Roots of Unity Group Scheme μ_n

generality.prompt: Is the construction stated over an arbitrary base scheme \(S\) and arbitrary positive integer \(n\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. \(S\) is any scheme; \(n\) is any positive integer (for \(n = 0\) we recover \(\mathbb{G}_m\)).

nodes.title: Hom Into Spec via Global Sections (Spec ⊣ Γ Adjunction)

generality.prompt: Does the statement apply to arbitrary schemes T over Spec R, not only affine T?
generality.verdict: Yes. This is the crux: the bijection holds for every T (not necessarily affine), because the target is affine. The bijection is natural in T.

nodes.title: Special Linear Group Scheme SL_n

spans.note: SL_n as the kernel of the determinant character on GL_n.
SL_n as a closed subgroup scheme of GL_n via the determinant.

generality.prompt: Is SL_n defined as a group scheme over an arbitrary base, not just over a field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The determinant is a morphism of group schemes over any base, so SL_n = ker(det) is a flat closed subgroup scheme of GL_n over Z, hence over any base scheme.

nodes.title: Special Orthogonal Group Scheme SO_n

spans.note: Orthogonal and special orthogonal groups as group schemes preserving a quadratic form.

generality.prompt: Is SO_n defined for quadratic forms over an arbitrary base ring, including in characteristic 2?
generality.verdict: Mostly yes. In characteristic not 2, SO_n = ker(det: O_n -> {±1}) is smooth. In characteristic 2, the orthogonal group requires a separate theory via quadratic forms (not symmetric bilinear forms, which degenerate). The Zariski-closure definition still gives a group scheme but smoothness requires the form to be non-degenerate in the relevant sense.

nodes.title: Symplectic Group Scheme Sp_{2n}

spans.note: Sp_{2n} as the isometry group of a standard symplectic form.

generality.prompt: Is Sp_{2n} defined as a flat affine group scheme over Z, not just over a field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The symplectic form J is defined over Z and the condition g^T J g = J is a closed subscheme condition, giving a smooth group scheme over Z.

nodes.title: Trivial Group Scheme over a Base

generality.prompt: Is the trivial group scheme defined over an arbitrary base \(S\)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction is functorial in \(S\) and does not depend on \(S\) being affine, of finite type, or over a field.

nodes.title: Trivial Representation as a Comodule

generality.prompt: Does the trivial comodule construction require a Hopf algebra?
generality.verdict: No. A bialgebra is enough: the coaction uses the group-like element \(1\), and the axioms use \(\Delta(1)=1\otimes 1\) and \(\varepsilon(1)=1\).
